title_en: BY.O v. Yushang Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over jurisdiction over a service contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: Although the parties agreed on two dispute resolution methods, arbitration and litigation, for the same dispute, if the agreement explicitly stipulates, or the content of the agreement indicates, that the arbitration method should be applied first and then the litigation method, it constitutes an 'arbitration-first-then-litigation' agreement. In foreign-related civil cases, the law applicable to the validity of such an 'arbitration-first-then-litigation' agreement shall be accurately determined. Where the arbitration-first clause is found to be legal and valid under the law that should apply to it, and given that the subsequent litigation clause is invalid because it violates the legal system of the forum state, i.e., China, regarding the finality and bindingness of arbitration awards, the invalidity of the subsequent litigation clause does not affect the validity of the arbitration-first clause. Therefore, it should be held that in a foreign-related 'arbitration-first-then-litigation' agreement, the arbitration clause is valid and the litigation clause is invalid.

full_text_en:
BY.O v. Yushang Group Co., Ltd. — Service Contract Dispute

Jurisdiction Objection Case

【Ruling Summary】

Where the parties have agreed on both arbitration and litigation as dispute resolution methods for the same dispute, but the agreement expressly provides, or the content of the agreement indicates, that arbitration should be applied first and litigation thereafter, such an agreement constitutes an "arbitration first, litigation later" agreement. In foreign-related civil cases, the law applicable to the validity of the "arbitration first, litigation later" agreement shall be accurately determined. Where the arbitration clause is found to be legal and valid under the law applicable to it, and the subsequent litigation clause is invalid because it violates the court's local legal system, i.e., China's system of final and binding arbitration awards, the invalidity of the subsequent litigation clause does not affect the validity of the prior arbitration clause. Therefore, it shall be determined that in a foreign-related "arbitration first, litigation later" agreement, the arbitration clause is valid and the litigation clause is invalid.

Plaintiff: BY.O (formerly BUY.O), domiciled at: Washington Street, Paris, French Republic (Washington 75008 Paris).

Representative: Marc DEBETS, Chief Executive Officer of the company.

Defendant: Yushang Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Yin Cheng Zhong Road, China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone.

Legal Representative: Shi Lei, General Manager of the company.

The plaintiff, BY.O, filed a lawsuit with the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai due to a service contract dispute with the defendant, Yushang Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yushang Company).

The plaintiff BY.O alleged: On May 4, 2015, the plaintiff and the defendant Yushang Company signed the "M&A Financial Advisory Service Agreement," agreeing that the defendant and its affiliates would engage the plaintiff to provide M&A financial advisory services, assisting the defendant and its affiliates in acquiring resort management companies, asset management companies, and luxury goods companies in the French region, among other matters. After the contract took effect, the plaintiff facilitated the defendant through its affiliates to sign a memorandum of understanding for the target acquisition project, determined the acquisition price and plan, signed the M&A transaction contract, and provided follow-up services. The plaintiff has performed the main obligations under the contract and issued invoices for the first, second, and third stage service fees to the defendant, which the defendant paid respectively. As for the fourth stage success fee of EUR 860,270, the plaintiff has issued an invoice to the defendant and repeatedly demanded payment, but the defendant has not paid to date. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court: 1. to order the defendant to pay the plaintiff the service fee of EUR 860,270; 2. to order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for the interest loss on the aforementioned service fee (calculated from December 16, 2016, to the date of actual payment, at an annual interest rate of 3.83%, based on the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR + 2%) as of December 16, 2016).

During the period for filing a statement of defense, the defendant Yushang Company raised a jurisdiction objection, arguing: First, the contract stipulates that any dispute or controversy arising from or relating to this agreement shall be first resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre. The above arbitration agreement is legal and valid, and this case should be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre. Second, since the parties have first chosen arbitration as the method of resolution, litigation should not be pursued; therefore, the agreement to resolve by litigation violates the principle of final arbitration awards and is invalid. In summary, this case should be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, and the court should rule to dismiss the plaintiff BY.O's lawsuit.

The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai found in the first instance:

In May 2015, the plaintiff BY.O (Party B) and the defendant Yushang Company (Party A) signed the "M&A Financial Advisory Service Agreement," stipulating that Party A and its affiliates would engage Party B to provide M&A financial advisory services, among other matters. Article 6 of the contract, regarding applicable law and jurisdiction, stipulated: 6.1 This agreement is entered into, executed, and interpreted in accordance with Chinese law; disputes arising from this agreement shall be governed by Chinese law. 6.2 Any dispute or controversy arising from or relating to this agreement (including disputes concerning the existence, validity, or termination of the terms of this agreement, or consequences of invalidity) shall first be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre. If the parties fail to reach an agreement on the arbitration result of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, either party shall have the right to submit the dispute to a competent commercial court at the domicile of Party A for resolution by litigation.

The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai held in the first instance:

In this case, the plaintiff BY.O is a foreign legal entity, and the plaintiff and the defendant signed the "M&A Financial Advisory Service Agreement," so it can be determined that the parties have established a foreign-related civil relationship, and this case is a foreign-related civil case. According to Article 6.1 of the contract, disputes arising from this agreement are governed by Chinese law, and both parties also recognize that the arbitration agreement is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the validity of the foreign-related arbitration clause in the contract shall be determined by applying the laws of the People's Republic of China.

Regarding whether this case should be submitted to the Singapore International Arbitration Centre for arbitration: First, according to Article 6.2 of the contract, any dispute or controversy arising from or relating to this agreement shall first be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre. This clause selects a clear and sole arbitration institution for dispute resolution. As commercial entities, the parties should be aware of the legal consequences of choosing arbitration for dispute resolution. Therefore, the above foreign-related arbitration clause is legal and valid, and this case should be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre. Second, Article 9 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Arbitration shall be conducted under the system of a single and final award. After an award is made, if a party applies for arbitration again for the same dispute or brings a lawsuit to a people's court, the arbitration commission or the people's court shall not accept it." The above law has been legally binding on the parties in this case since its effective date. Therefore, although the parties further stipulated in Article 6.2 of the contract that if they fail to reach an agreement on the arbitration result of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, either party shall have the right to submit the dispute to a competent commercial court at the domicile of Party A for resolution by litigation, this stipulation violates the legal provisions. Although the defendant Yushang Company's domicile is in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, which falls within the jurisdiction of this court, after the Singapore International Arbitration Centre renders an award on the civil dispute in this case, if a party brings a lawsuit to the people's court regarding the same dispute, regardless of whether the parties have a misunderstanding of the legal system of final arbitration awards, the people's court shall, in accordance with the above legal provisions, rule to dismiss the case. Therefore, this part of the stipulation has no legal effect. Third, the validity of the arbitration method clause and the litigation method clause shall be independent of each other. The invalidity of one part does not affect the validity of the other part. Therefore, although the litigation method clause is partially invalid, the arbitration method clause remains valid. Fourth, Article 6.2 of the contract stipulates that contractual disputes shall first be resolved through arbitration, and if the parties fail to reach an agreement on the arbitration result, they may resolve the dispute by litigation. However, these two methods are not parallel; the emphasis is on first resolving through arbitration. This is not an "arbitration or litigation" agreement, nor does it fall under the circumstance where the parties agree that disputes may be submitted to an arbitration commission for arbitration or to a people's court for litigation. Therefore, the foreign-related arbitration clause is legal and valid and should not be deemed invalid. In summary, the defendant's jurisdiction objection is established. This case should be submitted to the Singapore International Arbitration Centre for arbitration, and the plaintiff BY.O's lawsuit should be dismissed.

Accordingly, the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Article 18 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, Article 124(2) and Article 127(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 9(1) and Article 16 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 208(3) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a ruling on July 10, 2020:

I. The jurisdiction objection raised by the defendant, Yushang Group Co., Ltd., in this case is established;

II. The lawsuit filed by the plaintiff BY.O is dismissed.

BY.O, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, contending: The provision in Article 6.2 of the agreement involved in this case violates the basic principle of "final arbitration awards" and constitutes an "arbitration or litigation" clause, which should be deemed invalid; BY.O accordingly requested the revocation of the original ruling and a ruling that this case be heard by the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai.

After trial and upon review by the Shanghai High People's Court, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

This case is a foreign-related civil case. The provision in Article 6.2 of the "M&A Financial Advisory Service Agreement" involved in this case, stating "shall first be resolved through arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre," clearly prioritizes arbitration over litigation regarding the dispute resolution methods. It selects a specific, clear, and sole arbitration institution and does not have the characteristic of choosing between "arbitration or litigation." Therefore, the court recognizes the arbitration clause. As for the parties' further stipulation that "if the parties fail to reach an agreement on the arbitration result of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, either party shall have the right to submit the dispute to a competent commercial court at the domicile of Party A for resolution by litigation," this does not comply with Article 9(1) of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "arbitration shall be conducted under the system of a single and final award," and violates the basic principle that arbitration excludes court jurisdiction. Therefore, this stipulation shall be deemed invalid. This case shall be submitted to the Singapore International Arbitration Centre for arbitration. The original ruling dismissing the appellant BY.O's lawsuit is legally sound and is affirmed.

Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 170(1)(i) and Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a ruling on October 29, 2020:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
